questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe to do so.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars can disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars can disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars are hidden from the driver's view or too close for safe stopping and turning. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and cross the intersection safely.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and cross the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spot before moving back into your lane.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down, check for other traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent will:

options.text: Have no effect on your driving.
Not put other drivers at risk.
Double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your speed steady while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if you see one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if you see one.
questions.explanation: At this railroad crossing sign, you should look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane is ending.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. You should slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded areas. Water can hide hazards even if it looks shallow. Find another route instead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Make sudden, unplanned lane changes.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sudden, unplanned lane changes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for vehicles. Always signal your intention to change lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
As your speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds greatly increase the chance of death in a crash. Speed also affects how far it takes to stop, so increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
More slowly than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge at or near the speed of freeway traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you should:

options.text: The pedestrian must give you the right-of-way.
You must give them the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use guide dogs or white canes. You must yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb
The lane nearest the center of the street
The lane nearest the right curb

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb
questions.explanation: When making a left turn, use the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers
Drive closer to the car in front of you
Drive carefully and do not stare at the construction

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not stare at the construction
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things. Staring at construction causes traffic congestion. Keep your eyes on the road.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn on:

options.text: Your dashboard lights
Your parking lights
Your headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when it is hard for others to see you. Use your low beam headlights when you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly
Pump the brakes
Apply the brakes firmly

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while driving, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas and using light braking.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit
Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: You may legally block an intersection:

options.text: If you entered on a green light
During rush hour traffic
Never

questions.correctAnswerText: Never
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn is allowed here
A left turn is allowed only after stopping
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn is allowed here
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic that could cause a crash
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right
Always slow down and go without stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to cross traffic that could cause a crash
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let crossing or merging vehicles go first. Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see clearly, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic
Stay further back from the car in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay further back from the car in front of you
questions.explanation: In dark or bad weather, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards you cannot see.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line
Not allowed from either direction
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to make sure the next lane is clear. Looking over your shoulder helps you see your blind spot and check for vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles.

questions.question: The speed limit near a school crossing is:

options.text: 10 mph
15 mph
25 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph
questions.explanation: When no other speed limit is posted, drive 15 mph near school crossings.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: A construction zone is ahead
Passing is not allowed from either direction
Passing is allowed from either direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and lane until it passes
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes
Pull over to the curb or edge and stop until it passes

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge and stop until it passes
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge.
